content.thinking:
I should check the relevant tools before responding further. Under the Act, a tenant on a periodic tenancy must give at least two months' notice, so one month isn't sufficient—if notice is given on 10 October 2026, the earliest valid end date would be 10 December 2026, unless the landlord agrees in writing to an earlier date.

Shortening the notice period would require a surrender agreement, and I shouldn't make promises about the deposit or keys since the tenancy and rent obligations continue until the agreed end date, with deposit disputes going through ADR. Since ending the tenancy early is ultimately the landlord's call, I should request landlord approval from Ben, reply to the tenant explaining the two-month notice requirement, and schedule a follow-up rather than escalating this as a legal matter.

arguments.body: Hi Tom, thanks for letting us know, and congratulations on the new job. Since 1 May 2026 the notice a tenant needs to give is two months, so one month's notice unfortunately doesn't end the tenancy on 10 November. Counting from today (10 October), the earliest end date is 10 December 2026, and rent stays payable until then. You can finish sooner only if your landlord agrees in writing. I'm asking him now whether he will accept 10 November, and I'll update you by Wednesday 14 October. Please don't treat 10 November as agreed until you have that in writing. Keys: please don't send or drop them yet. We'll confirm the handover place and time once the end date is settled. Deposit: it's protected with mydeposits. After the tenancy ends and the flat is checked, we'll agree any deductions with you and the landlord, and return the rest; we can't give a date until the end date is settled. If you'd rather confirm the 10 December end date, just reply and say so.

arguments.decision_needed: Tenant Tom Achterberg (Flat 2, 5 Navarino Road) gave one month's notice on 10 Oct 2026 to leave on 10 Nov. That is not valid; two months is required, so the tenancy ends 10 Dec 2026 at the earliest. Do you agree in writing to a shorter end date of 10 Nov? Please reply by Tuesday 13 October.
options: Keep the legal end date of 10 December 2026 (recommended unless you have a new tenant ready)
Agree in writing to end on 10 November 2026 (rent stops then; you may lose a month's rent if not re-let)
Agree to another date in between

arguments.purpose: Chase Ben Hartley for decision on early end date for T-1050; update tenant either way

I should check the relevant tools before responding further. Under the Act, a tenant on a periodic tenancy must give at least two months' notice, so one month isn't sufficient—if notice is given on 10 October 2026, the earliest valid end date would be 10 December 2026, unless the landlord agrees in writing to an earlier date.

Shortening the notice period would require a surrender agreement, and I shouldn't make promises about the deposit or keys since the tenancy and rent obligations continue until the agreed end date, with deposit disputes going through ADR. Since ending the tenancy early is ultimately the landlord's call, I should request landlord approval from Ben, reply to the tenant explaining the two-month notice requirement, and schedule a follow-up rather than escalating this as a legal matter.

arguments.body: Hi Tom, thanks for letting us know, and congratulations on the new job. Since 1 May 2026 the notice a tenant needs to give is two months, so one month's notice unfortunately doesn't end the tenancy on 10 November. Counting from today (10 October), the earliest end date is 10 December 2026, and rent stays payable until then. You can finish sooner only if your landlord agrees in writing. I'm asking him now whether he will accept 10 November, and I'll update you by Wednesday 14 October. Please don't treat 10 November as agreed until you have that in writing. Keys: please don't send or drop them yet. We'll confirm the handover place and time once the end date is settled. Deposit: it's protected with mydeposits. After the tenancy ends and the flat is checked, we'll agree any deductions with you and the landlord, and return the rest; we can't give a date until the end date is settled. If you'd rather confirm the 10 December end date, just reply and say so.
